answer: Each identity holds one state-issued drone-operator certificate, registry-checked and bound to one airframe by serial number. Flight logs with nadir-view imagery follow each survey — orchard canopy, coastline — matched to airframe and pilot; one certificate backs one identity, duplicates rejected. One costs an exam, 40 hours, 900 units and 120 days; 100 fakes: 90,000 units, 12,000 days. Cheapest cheat: renting an operator for 600 units a flight — the lender surrenders their own certificate, forged logs fail serial checks, and a borrowed drone over a tidal inlet needs its own operator.
